metadata.description: Workflow primitives that keep AI-assisted coding from losing the threads that matter — /threads:retro reviews a session, /threads:process-review reads what accumulates across sessions.

plugins.name: threads
plugins.description: Process tooling for Claude Code — two commands, one loop. /threads:retro reviews a session as process telemetry (how it happened, not whether the code is correct), by default via a fresh-context sub-agent that audits the observable record cold; a second fresh sub-agent places findings in the repo's process docs, biased to amend before add, and keys them against a retro log so "adopt if it recurs" is measured rather than hoped for. Retro captures findings to that log instead of applying them at the session's most expensive moment. /threads:process-review adjudicates what's pending, reads what accumulated across sessions — process-shaped commits, or process-doc churn as a fallback — surfaces reconciliation and structural candidates, and sweeps stable process/workflow docs for negative-space drift the churn signal can't see. No hooks; retro closes with a ripeness nudge instead. First runs bootstrap by inspection and negotiate conventions; nothing is applied without recorded consent.

plugins.name: slices
plugins.description: Day-one slice pipeline — /slices:capture files one-concern, low-trust stubs the moment work is discovered; /slices:draft promotes a stub into a plan that re-verifies the capture's claims and ends in a review digest (shape + at most five tension points); /slices:check hands the plan to a fresh-context adversary told only its path, and no plan is implement-ready until it survives. Rung-one by design: the artifacts are the contract, and later hardening only appends to them.
